author: claude
author_note: Authored by a Claude-family model (the same family as the evaluated agents); see CASES.md for the family-bias risk. All products, studies and journals are fictional; the fixture gives no real medical advice.
severity_rubric: R5: critical only when a named criterion is met (not indexable; required unique element absent; primary task fails for some users; user deceived or charged a wrong payable amount); major = measurable harm to ranking, access, trust or conversion; minor = polish or reachable another way.

defects.title: The article claims the cream cleared flare-ups in 93 % of users within two weeks, but its own reference [1] reports 43 % improvement at 12 weeks with no 2-week assessment.
defects.evidence: article.html: "cleared flare-ups in 93 % of users within two weeks [1]"; references.html #ref-1 summary: "At 12 weeks 43 % of participants reported improvement ... no participant was assessed at 2 weeks".
defects.fix: Restate the claim as the source reports it (43 % improvement at 12 weeks, n = 84, open-label) or remove it.
defects.rationale: The citation marker makes the sentence look sourced; the contradiction is only visible after opening the separate reference file.

detector.example: 1. [major] [content] The 93 % within two weeks claim misrepresents reference [1], which reports 43 % improvement at 12 weeks and no 2-week assessment.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: The FAQ answer on pregnancy ("Stop all barrier creams") contradicts the body, which says barrier creams are generally considered compatible with pregnancy.
defects.evidence: Body under #prescription: "generally considered compatible with pregnancy, but check with your clinician"; FAQ and FAQPage schema: "No. Stop all barrier creams during pregnancy."
defects.fix: Make the FAQ answer agree with the body (and the schema with both), after an editorial check of which statement is intended.
defects.rationale: The FAQ and its schema agree with each other, so a FAQ-to-schema check passes; the contradiction is with a sentence in a different section.

detector.example: 2. [major] [content] The FAQ says to stop all barrier creams during pregnancy while the body says they are generally compatible with pregnancy: a direct contradiction.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: The page promises a medical review but names no reviewer and gives no review date: the reviewer span is empty and the schema has no reviewedBy or lastReviewed.
defects.evidence: Medically reviewed by ; author box: "She is not a clinician"; MedicalWebPage node has no reviewedBy / lastReviewed / dateModified.
defects.fix: Name a qualified reviewer with credentials and a review date in the byline and in the MedicalWebPage schema, or remove the "Medically reviewed by" label.
defects.rationale: The label reads as a passed check; the empty span is invisible in a rendered view.

detector.example: 3. [major] [trust] "Medically reviewed by" is followed by an empty span and no review date; the schema has no reviewedBy or lastReviewed.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: The Article node's dateModified (2026-03-10) precedes its datePublished (2026-07-21), an impossible timeline.
defects.fix: Set dateModified to the real last-edit date on or after 21 July 2026.
defects.rationale: Both values are valid dates; only their order is wrong.

detector.example: 4. [major] [seo] dateModified 2026-03-10 is earlier than datePublished 2026-07-21, so the freshness data is impossible.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: The head declares two canonical URLs that differ, so search engines receive conflicting canonical signals.
defects.fix: Keep one canonical, the URL that og:url and the references include use (/guides/barrier-creams/).
defects.rationale: The first canonical is correct, so a reader who stops at the first match passes it.

detector.example: 5. [major] [seo] Two canonical tags with different URLs are declared in the head.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: A sponsored product card placed directly under the prescription section claims the balm "works just as well as prescription Lumacort for weeping flares, with no appointment needed", pushing a purchase through a deceptive medical equivalence (criterion: user pushed by deception).
defects.evidence: .sponsor-card inside #prescription's section: "works just as well as prescription Lumacort for weeping flares, with no appointment needed. From $14." The body two paragraphs above says weeping flares need a clinician.
defects.fix: Remove the equivalence claim and move the card out of the prescription section (or drop it from a YMYL page).
defects.rationale: The card is correctly labelled Sponsored and its link carries rel=sponsored, so compliance checks on the link pass; the harm is the claim and its placement.

any: (sponsor|velvetine|balm|card)[^\n]{0,120}(just as well|as well as prescription|equivalen|no appointment|replace[^\n]{0,20}prescription|instead of (a )?prescription)
detector.example: 6. [critical] [commercial] The sponsored Velvetine card under the prescription section claims it works just as well as prescription Lumacort with no appointment needed: a deceptive medical equivalence that pushes a purchase.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: The self-check list conveys its triage level by colour only (green, amber, red dots) with no text or accessible name.
defects.evidence: , dot-amber, dot-red are empty spans; the meaning of each colour is explained only in a paragraph below.
defects.fix: Add visible or visually hidden text ("Green: self-care", "Amber: book an appointment", "Red: see a clinician this week") to each item.
defects.rationale: The explanatory paragraph makes the list look documented, but the per-item mapping still depends on seeing the colour.

detector.example: 7. [major] [a11y] The self-check list signals triage level by colour-only dots (empty spans) with no text alternative.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: The "On this page" link to #causes points at no element (the heading id is what-causes-flares), so that jump link does nothing; the section is still reachable by scrolling.
defects.evidence: <a href="#causes"> in .toc; the heading is <h2 id="what-causes-flares">.
defects.fix: Change the link to #what-causes-flares (or the id to causes).
defects.rationale: Four of five jump links work, and the target is reachable another way, which is why the rubric rates it minor; agents tend to rate any broken link major.

detector.example: 8. [minor] [a11y] The on-page link #causes targets no element; the heading id is what-causes-flares.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: The steroid-sparing claim cites reference [3], but the reference list contains only two entries, so the claim has no source.
defects.evidence: article.html: "documented steroid-sparing effect ... [3]" linking to references.html#ref-3; references.html lists #ref-1 and #ref-2 only.
defects.fix: Add the missing reference or remove the claim.
defects.rationale: The marker looks like every other citation; only counting the entries in the other file reveals the gap.

detector.example: 9. [major] [content] The steroid-sparing claim cites [3], but references.html lists only two entries, so the citation is dangling.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: The three application-step photos carry the placeholder alt text "image", so the steps' visual instructions are not described.
defects.evidence: and the same for steps 2 and 3.
defects.fix: Write descriptive alt text for each step (or alt="" if the captions fully describe them and the images are decorative).
defects.rationale: Alt attributes are present and non-empty, so automated checks pass; the value is meaningless.

detector.example: 10. [major] [a11y] The three application-step photos use the placeholder alt="image", which describes nothing.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.
